display.title: Episode 367: The Return of Yehudah, Chapter 12 (Rosh Chodesh Adar II)
display.summary_short: A double portion of joy on Rosh Chodesh Adar II, a class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park says the Shema, and the village rabbi asks Yehudah to marry his daughter.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the first day of Rosh Chodesh Adar II 5749. Uncle Yossi explains that a leap year brings a double portion of 'increase in joy', and after a month of practice in Adar I it is time for even more simcha, starting with the Hakochainik march. A third-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park leads the Shema. In the story, Yehudah, now the village melamed, is loved by his students and becomes the talk of the town. The rabbi, who has watched how he davens, learns and conducts himself, asks him to marry his daughter Esther. Yehudah thinks of the secret message sewn into his talis katan, to be opened only under the chuppah, and asks for time to think it over. In the mailbox, a boy asks how to join Tzivos Hashem, and Uncle Yossi explains what new members receive, why it is never too early to join, the bundle of sticks that cannot be broken together, and how children will lead the parade out of exile when Moshiach comes. The show ends with a spectacular Shiviti sign shaped like an Aron Kodesh and Shabbos times.
display.lesson: Together, like a bundle of sticks, the Jewish people cannot be broken; and in Adar we keep adding joy.
